candidate.answerReason: Among 126 equally likely dot-removal and top-face pairs, 12·4+9·2=66 leave an odd number of dots on top. The probability is 66/126=11/21.

methods.label: Count dot-removal and top-face pairs
methods.explanation:
The removed dot is chosen uniformly, so count individual dots rather than treating the six removal faces as equally likely. The die has \(1+2+3+4+5+6=21\) dots. For each removed dot, the six physical faces are equally likely to land on top. Thus there are \(21\cdot6=126\) equally likely pairs consisting of a removed dot and a top face.

There are \(2+4+6=12\) dots on the originally even faces. Removing any one of these changes that face to odd, leaving four odd faces available for the roll. These removals give \(12\cdot4=48\) favorable pairs.

The remaining \(1+3+5=9\) dots lie on originally odd faces. Removing one changes its face to even, leaving only two odd faces. This includes removing the lone dot from the one-dot face, since zero is even. These removals give \(9\cdot2=18\) favorable pairs.

The two cases cover all removals without overlap, so the probability is
\[\frac{48+18}{126}=\frac{66}{126}=\frac{11}{21},\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses an elementary equally likely sample space and addition and multiplication counting.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is an exact probability from a finite equally likely model. The method constructs dot-and-face pairs and uses combined counting for the two disjoint removal cases. Equal-likelihood reasoning and parity support the solution. Conditional-probability formulas are not used.

review.mathematicalCheck: There are 126 equally likely removed-dot and top-face pairs. The 12 removals from even faces each permit four odd top faces; the nine removals from odd faces each permit two. Thus the favorable count is 66 and the probability is \(66/126=11/21\). Zero dots is correctly treated as even.
review.levelCheck: The elementary sample-space argument explains equal likelihood, the two cases and their multiplicities.
